jobs.title: Director Enterprise Architecture
jobs.description:
Director, Enterprise Architecture

Salary:
$200,000–$230,000 annually
Location:
Canada
Work Arrangement:
Hybrid – 2–3 days in office per week
Employment Type:
Full-time, Permanent
Department:
Technology Services
Industry:
Law

Position Overview
Our client, a leading national law firm, is seeking a Director, Enterprise Architecture to join its Technology Services team.
This newly created leadership position will lead the development and governance of the firm's enterprise architecture, aligning business capabilities, applications, data, integration and infrastructure with its overall business strategy.
The Director will translate business priorities into a practical architectural vision and roadmap that enables exceptional client service, operational effectiveness, innovation and secure, sustainable growth.
A key priority will be modernizing the firm's enterprise data environment, improving data quality and advancing enterprise-wide AI adoption.
The successful candidate will bring a combination of strategic leadership, deep technical expertise and the ability to lead and collaborate with a highly experienced team of architects and technology professionals.

Key Responsibilities
Enterprise Architecture & Strategic Roadmaps
Define and maintain an enterprise architecture vision and principles across business and IT domains, tailored to the organization's size, complexity and operating model.
Collaborate with business units to translate business needs and current-state assessments into target-state designs and multi-year roadmaps.
Assess application and technology portfolios to identify duplication, technical debt, dependencies and modernization opportunities.
Shape investment plans and business cases, presenting options, costs, benefits and implementation trade-offs.
Align roadmaps with portfolio planning, organizational capacity and change readiness, balancing immediate needs with long-term outcomes.
Provide strategic direction for enterprise data architecture, data quality and data modernization initiatives.

Architecture Governance, Design & Collaboration
Establish consistent national architecture standards and reusable design patterns.
Lead architecture reviews, document decisions, manage exceptions and escalate material risks through appropriate governance forums.
Guide solution design throughout delivery, ensuring interoperability, scalability, resilience and alignment with enterprise standards.
Partner with security, privacy, risk and data stakeholders to embed confidentiality, information protection, records requirements, human oversight and responsible AI controls into designs.
Evaluate third-party platforms and sourcing options for architectural fit, integration requirements, vendor risk, lifecycle sustainability and total cost of ownership.
Resolve cross-domain design issues with delivery and operations leaders, ensuring clear ownership of risk mitigation and implementation decisions.
Report on standards adoption, technical debt reduction, reuse and roadmap progress.
Provide architectural thought leadership and promote knowledge sharing across technical communities.
Foster a positive, collaborative culture across the architecture team and its partners.
Act as an ambassador for enterprise architecture and the IT function, helping stakeholders understand its value and services.

Data Modernization, AI & Technology Enablement
Lead initiatives to assess, clean up and modernize complex enterprise data environments.
Establish sustainable data architecture standards and processes to improve data quality, consistency, accessibility and reliability.
Guide legacy modernization and integration to reduce technical debt and optimize the use of technologies.
Develop and advance the firm's enterprise AI strategy.
Collaborate with the AI Steering Committee to define secure and scalable architectures for AI and automation.
Evaluate pilots for business value, scalability and architectural fit, and guide successful initiatives into supported enterprise deployment.
Support the development of dashboards, enterprise reporting and actionable business insights.
Promote reuse of enterprise platforms to avoid fragmented tools and duplicated investment.

People Leadership & Financial Management
Lead, mentor and support a team of approximately 3–4 highly experienced technical professionals.
Provide strategic direction while maintaining the technical expertise necessary to guide and challenge architectural recommendations.
Serve as a trusted technical advisor to experienced architects and technology professionals.
Build trust, foster collaboration and establish alignment across the architecture team.
Introduce structured processes and sustainable technology implementation practices.
Manage the function's operating budget and support technology investment planning.
Build strong relationships with executive leadership and cross-functional business stakeholders.

Experience & Competencies
Minimum of 10 years of experience in solution, technology or enterprise architecture, with demonstrated experience architecting complex enterprise solutions.
Strong experience within a law firm or comparable professional services environment, with an understanding of client confidentiality, privacy, security, risk management and professional productivity.
Experience within large banking, insurance or comparable complex enterprise environments will also be considered.
Demonstrated experience assessing, improving and modernizing complex enterprise data environments.
Extensive experience designing enterprise solutions and platforms that meet security, availability, performance and resilience requirements.
Ability to collaborate with other architects and provide technical direction on complex, high-visibility initiatives involving multiple technology domains.
Demonstrated experience developing enterprise architecture roadmaps across applications, data, integration and infrastructure, aligned with business priorities and investment planning.
Experience guiding legacy modernization, cloud adoption and enterprise integration, including assessing third-party platforms and technology risks.
Experience evaluating AI-enabled solutions and automation, with attention to secure integration, information protection and responsible-use controls.
Demonstrated experience leading and developing highly technical teams.
Experience managing operating budgets and developing technology investment recommendations.
Excellent organizational and prioritization skills, with the ability to lead multiple complex initiatives while balancing changing business priorities.
Strong interpersonal skills, with the ability to build consensus, collaborate with senior business and technology stakeholders, and communicate architectural trade-offs.
High degree of initiative, independence and self-management.
Strong client-service orientation and the ability to translate stakeholder needs into effective technology solutions.
Highly developed analytical and problem-solving skills.

Technical Skills
Strong understanding of legal or comparable technology ecosystems, including:
Document and email management
Practice and financial management
Client and matter intake
Conflicts management
Records management
Knowledge management
eDiscovery
Time entry
Legal workflow platforms
Knowledge of leading professional services platforms and their architectural considerations, such as iManage, Aderant, Intapp, Microsoft 365, Copilot and comparable enterprise technologies.
Broad technical knowledge across enterprise applications, cloud platforms, infrastructure, data, integration, identity, security and end-user technologies.
Ability to assess architectural dependencies and trade-offs across multiple technology domains.

Education & Additional Qualifications
University degree or college diploma in Computer Science, Information Technology or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
Enterprise architecture certification or formal training in enterprise architecture frameworks, principles and practices.
Bilingualism in English and French is considered an asset.

Ideal Candidate
The ideal candidate is a collaborative, technically credible and forward-thinking technology leader who can balance enterprise-wide strategy with practical technical guidance.
They will bring the humility and interpersonal skills necessary to earn the trust of an established technical team, while introducing greater structure, strategic alignment and sustainable technology practices across the organization.
Previous experience within a large organization of approximately 1,000 or more employees is strongly preferred.

Why Join?
Competitive annual salary of $200,000–$230,000.
Flexible hybrid working environment.
Opportunity to shape a newly created strategic leadership position.
Executive-level support for AI adoption and technology modernization.
Opportunity to lead an established, highly experienced technical team.
Meaningful influence over the long-term technology direction of a leading national organization.

Job Description

What is the Opportunity?

The Director, CIAM Business Enablement will be responsible for leading the CIAM Business Enablement team, a new and growing group that matures and aligns Customer Identity and Access Management (CIAM) across the enterprise. You will lead the Product Quality Assurance (QA) and metrics teams and drive initiatives that strengthen CIAM maturity and remediation in response to an evolving customer identity threat landscape. Your scope includes business analysis and testing for CIAM products, integrations, and enhancements, as well as the metrics and reporting that give leadership visibility into CIAM risk and performance.

What will you do?

Lead and develop the Product QA and metrics teams.
Drive, lead, and participate in initiatives that advance CIAM maturity and remediation across the enterprise.
Engage stakeholders and partners in the Customer IAM Identity Governance Model (CLGM) to identify key CIAM metrics based on business needs, key risks, emerging threats, and regulatory changes, and maintain a data dictionary.
Regularly engage stakeholders to identify new metrics requirements and close existing visibility gaps.
Own and formalize CIAM first line of defense (1LOD) reporting requirements, including frequency and reporting dates, and work with other lines of defense to enable enterprise CIAM key indicator reporting.
Foster strong, collaborative relationships across functional areas.
Identify data sources, key data elements, and guide the development of automated data pipelines that provide leadership with continuous visibility.
Lead CIAM business analysis, QA and testing (including new product development, integrations, and enhancements), and enhancement backlog management to ensure consistent delivery.
Oversea and develop CLGM summary reports that identify deficiencies, technical debt, gaps, and underperforming metrics for leadership action

What do you need to succeed?

Must have:

Previous people management experience leading teams.
5+ years within a global financial organization, or knowledge of the financial IT industry.
10+ years of hands-on experience building reporting solutions using large, multi-source data sets.
5+ across the full data intelligence lifecycle, including data modelling, development, testing, documentation, and deployment.
Advanced SQL proficiency and a solid understanding of data warehouse concepts, including modelling.
Experience with Python and the ability to automate reports.
Hands-on experience building reports and dashboards from large, multi-source data sets using tools such as Tableau, Power BI, or Snowflake.
Product QA and testing experience, including test plans, defect management, and automation.
Strong analytical, presentation, and project management skills, with experience preparing senior management materials.
Excellent communication skills and the ability to work with stakeholders at all levels.
Highly organized, detail-oriented self-starter.
An undergraduate degree.

Nice to have:

Experience in identity and access management field.
Experience working in a global financial organization.
Project or program management experience.
Data science experience, and experience automating with AI and other tools

We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

jobs.description:
WOW 1 DAY PAINTING is at a pivotal point in its growth. We've just completed a brand refresh that launches across North America in Q1 2027, and we're looking for a Vice President, Marketing to make it a main driver of growth. Our goals are aggressive: double the business in the next three years, on the path to $100 million in system-wide revenue and a brand that triples in size over five to six years. This is a growth leadership role, not a traditional marketing role: you'll own business outcomes, not just marketing activities, and sit on the leadership team that decides how a franchise brand wins customers and new franchise partners.

About

We'll grow by going deeper in the markets we serve and by expanding into new ones through additional franchises, across residential and commercial (B2B) customers, with the mix expected to move toward about 60% residential and 40% commercial. You will:

Brand Relaunch & Digital Strategy

Lead the Q1 2027 North American launch of the refreshed brand and relaunched website.
Build the brand through video and digital content, resetting the digital strategy across paid, earned, shared, and owned (PESO) channels.
Build an internal content production capability alongside vendor partners.

Full-Funnel Customer Growth & Retention

Design, develop and manage a full-funnel growth strategy connecting customer acquisition, retention, and lifetime value across brand, performance, referral, and loyalty marketing.
Drive performance marketing, with a focus on Meta and YouTube.
Expand the referral program by leveraging an industry-leading customer experience.

Franchise Expansion & Local Execution

Lead franchise development marketing to attract new franchise partners and expand across North America.
Balance national brand strategy with local execution by planning and running marketing alongside franchise partners to grow leads, customers, revenue, and franchisee profitability.

Commercial (B2B) & Residential Market Growth

Grow commercial (B2B) revenue alongside residential revenue with the leadership team, helping shift the business mix toward ~60% residential and 40% commercial.
Deepen presence in existing markets while expanding into new territories.

Analytics, Operations & Team Leadership

Own measurement, attribution, and AI-enabled marketing operations.
Establish clear KPIs and scorecards to hold agencies, franchise partners, and the internal team accountable for results.
Build and lead a team of in-brand marketers and vendor partners.

This role is based in Vancouver or Toronto, with a hybrid work model.

About You

You're a customer- and partner-minded, full-funnel growth leader who combines strategic thinking with strong execution, builds accountable teams and partners, and knows how to scale both brand and performance across a franchise system. You bring:

10+ years in marketing, including 5+ years leading multiple marketing functions across multiple locations.
Proven full-funnel growth across paid, shared, owned channels including programs that turn customers into repeat business and advocates.
Multi-location and franchise systems expertise: you balance national brand strategy with local execution, franchisee engagement and profitability, and you know how to market to attract new franchise partners.
Brand building through video and digital content, with experience building an internal content production capability.
Performance marketing expertise, across all digital channels.
Measurement, attribution and AI-enabled marketing operations, with ownership of data and outcomes through KPIs, business scorecards (BSC), OKRs and agency oversight, and revenue operations experience (CRM, funnel, automation).
A commercial orientation: you turn business objectives into strategy, align people, technology, process and investment, and have grown B2B revenue alongside residential or consumer revenue.
Exceptional leadership, influence and communication: you build high-performing teams and create alignment and accountability across agencies, franchise partners and stakeholders.
A bachelor's degree in marketing, business or a related field (an MBA is an asset), and an understanding of CASL and CAN-SPAM.

The Brand

WOW 1 DAY PAINTING is a fast-growing house painting franchise and part of O2E Brands, the parent company of the hugely successful 1-800-GOT-JUNK?. Our franchise partners deliver an industry-leading customer experience, and we've just completed a brand refresh that launches across North America in Q1 2027, backed by the digital presence and the team to double the business in three years.

O2E Brands has been voted one of the Best Workplaces in Canada 15 times. When we say It's All About People, we mean it: our hybrid model helps us get together to collaborate, celebrate and connect, with flexibility where it makes sense for you.

What's In It For You

A seat on the leadership team and the chance to shape the growth of a brand.
Long-term incentive opportunities.
Salary Range: $160,000-190,000, plus bonus, plus profit share.
Extended health and dental, professional development programs, and wellness initiatives.

jobs.title: Director, Trading Market Risk - Global Equities
jobs.description:
We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients.

At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute.

To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com

What You'll Be Doing

Capital Markets Risk Management provides independent oversight across CIBC’s trading businesses to support strong, disciplined risk management. As a Director, Trading Floor Market Risk Management, you’ll provide independent market risk oversight for the Global Equities trading desks. You’ll build a deep understanding of trading and hedging strategies, provide effective challenge to the desks, and perform daily and periodic monitoring of positions, risk, profit and loss (P&L), and capital. You’ll proactively monitor market developments to assess potential risk impacts and partner with the Stress team to enhance stress scenario analysis for the Global Equities business. You’ll support the Head of Trading Market Risk for Global Equities and work closely with risk managers globally to deliver timely, accurate risk and product analysis to senior management. You’ll also lead initiatives to enhance risk measurement, including improvements to internal risk measures and Fundamental Review of the Trading Book (FRTB) capital metrics.

At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. You'll have the flexibility to manage your work activities within a hybrid work arrangement where you'll spend 2-3 days per week on-site, while other days will be remote.

How You'll Succeed

Risk oversight and communication - Monitor trading activity, limit utilization, and key risk exposures across the Global Equities trading desks. Ensure timely communication of changes in desk profit and loss (P&L) and risk, and deliver clear, insightful analysis to senior management and other key stakeholders.
Effective challenge and risk management - Provide effective challenge on trading strategies, positions, and risk management practices. Identify material market risk factors and emerging risk, and apply sound judgment to support strong second line oversight.
Partnership across functions - Build strong working relationships with partners across Capital Markets Risk, Trading, Finance, Technology, Quantitative Risk, Market Risk Solutions, and Limit Monitoring and Governance. Work collaboratively to improve reporting, processes, and risk transparency.
Risk framework enhancement - Partner with the Stress team to strengthen scenario analysis and support enhancements to the broader market risk framework for the Global Equities business.
Measurement and process improvement - Lead initiatives to enhance internal risk measures and FRTB capital metrics. Use your quantitative, database, and coding skills to streamline and automate oversight processes, reporting, and ad hoc analysis.
Regulatory and market expertise - Maintain deep knowledge of capital markets products, valuation approaches, sensitivities, risk models, and regulatory developments affecting market risk and capital frameworks, with a focus on Global Equities and equity derivatives.

Who You Are

You have deep market risk experience. You bring 7+ years of experience in market risk, trading, or a related risk discipline. You also have strong knowledge of capital markets products, particularly Global Equities, including structured notes, equity exotics, equity options, and equity financing.
You have the right academic foundation. You hold a degree in Quantitative Finance, Business, Finance, Economics, Engineering, Statistics, or a related field. A master’s degree is an asset.
You are technically strong and analytically minded. You are digitally savvy and embrace innovative solutions, including AI and evolving technologies. You’re comfortable using tools such as Python, SQL, Bloomberg API, and other programming or database platforms. You use data and technology to improve oversight, reporting, and risk analysis.
Your influence makes a difference. You can translate complex topics into clear, actionable insights for a range of stakeholders. You also have the project leadership skills to drive initiatives across multiple partners.
You act like an owner. You have strong attention to detail, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills. You take ownership, show initiative, and consistently deliver high-quality work.
Values matter to you. You bring your real self to work and you live our values – trust, teamwork, and accountability.

What CIBC Offers

At CIBC, your goals are a priority. We start with your strengths and ambitions as an employee and strive to create opportunities to tap into your potential. We aspire to give you a career, rather than just a paycheck.

We work to recognize you in meaningful, personalized ways including a competitive salary, incentive pay, banking benefits, a benefits program*, defined benefit pension plan*, an employee share purchase plan, a vacation offering, wellbeing support, and MomentMakers, our social, points-based recognition program.
Our spaces and technological toolkit will make it simple to bring together great minds to create innovative solutions that make a difference for our clients.
We cultivate a culture where you can express your ambition through initiatives like Purpose Day; a paid day off dedicated for you to use to invest in your growth and development.

jobs.title: Product Design Director
jobs.description:
About YPO

YPO is a global leadership community of over 35,000 chief executives from more than 140 countries. YPO brings together extraordinary leaders who are committed to becoming better leaders and better people. The organization provides a platform for the leaders to connect, learn, and grow through shared experiences, rich learning programs, and meaningful relationships. Members benefit from a supportive community that fosters personal, business, family and community growth.

Supporting these members is a world-class management team of more than 450 associates, spanning over 25 countries. Our organization is based in Dallas, Texas, with many associates working virtually and outside of the United States. Together, our team of global associates works to create a truly Only-in-YPO experience for our members.

Location & Onsite Expectations

Candidates based in the Dallas–Fort Worth area are strongly preferred. This role will require an onsite presence, with the specific number of days per week to be determined. Highly qualified candidates based elsewhere in the U.S. and Canada may also be considered. C andidates in Canada must reside in British Columbia, Ontario, Alberta or Nova Scotia
as YPO is not an employer in other Canadian provinces.

About the Opportunity

At YPO, we're reimagining how technology can better connect, engage, and empower leaders across our global community.

We're seeking an experienced Product Design Director to build and shape our product design function from the ground up, establishing a unified design vision across our evolving digital ecosystem.

This is an opportunity to make a lasting impact on how our members experience YPO. You'll define the design principles, systems, and standards that bring consistency across our platforms, guide the evolution of our mobile and digital experiences, and help shape how AI creates more intuitive, personalized, and meaningful interactions.

We're looking for a leader who combines deep UX and product design expertise with the ability to build teams, influence product strategy, and turn complex challenges into thoughtful, scalable solutions. Someone with a strong point of view who can balance innovation with execution, navigate competing priorities, and bring stakeholders together around a shared vision.

Reporting to our Chief Product Officer, you'll partner closely with Product, Engineering, Data, and business leaders to establish the foundation for design excellence at YPO while remaining hands-on as the function grows.

What You'll Do

Build and Lead Our Design Function: Establish and grow an in-house product design team, developing the frameworks, processes, and practices that enable high-quality design across multiple product teams.
Establish a Unified Design Vision: Define a cohesive design strategy, scalable design systems, and consistent interaction standards across YPO's web, mobile, and digital experiences.
Shape Our Digital Future: Guide the evolution of our mobile application ecosystem and digital platforms, translating emerging opportunities into intuitive, connected member experiences.
Champion Research-Driven Design: Lead user research, usability testing, and persona development, using qualitative insights and product analytics to identify problems, validate solutions, and inform product decisions.
Advance AI-First Experiences: Help define how AI enhances the member experience through conversational interfaces, intelligent agents, personalization, and adaptive design, with an emphasis on transparency, trust, and user control.
Influence Product Direction: Partner with Product, Engineering, Data, and business stakeholders to navigate competing priorities, advocate for user-centered decisions, and align teams around a shared vision.
Lead as a Player-Coach: Combine strategic leadership with hands-on design, prototyping, critique, and problem-solving while mentoring designers and elevating the team's capabilities.
Drive Design Excellence: Champion accessibility, thoughtful interactions, and measurable product outcomes, ensuring experiences are scalable, inclusive, and consistent with YPO's mission.

What We're Looking For

10+ years of product design experience, including 5+ years leading and developing design teams, ideally at the Director level.
Demonstrated success building or scaling product design functions, establishing design systems, and setting design standards across complex digital products.
Deep expertise in UX, interaction design, user research, usability testing, and translating customer needs into intuitive, scalable solutions.
Strong understanding of Apple's Human Interface Guidelines and Google's Material Design principles, with experience designing for iOS, Android, and web platforms.

Passion Dental Group is looking for an experienced Regional Director to lead and support our Anytime Clinics across the Hamilton area. We’re seeking a hands-on leader with strong dental operations experience and a proven ability to build teams, develop leaders and improve clinic performance.

You understand that successful clinics depend on effective operations, engaged people and accessible, patient-centred care. You know how to identify what’s working, address what needs improvement and bring teams together around clear priorities. Whether you’re coaching a Clinic Manager, partnering with a Doctor or working through an operational challenge, you bring a practical, collaborative approach that builds trust and delivers results.

As Regional Director, you’ll oversee the operational performance of our Hamilton-area Anytime Clinics, working closely with Clinic Managers, Doctors and Support Office partners to strengthen teams, improve day-to-day operations and support sustainable growth.

You’ll help each clinic succeed by understanding the people, processes and opportunities behind its results. You’ll provide clear direction, establish accountability and ensure clinic leaders have the support and tools they need to lead effectively.

Within the Anytime Clinics environment, you’ll help teams balance patient access and responsiveness with effective scheduling, staffing and consistent service. Your focus will be on helping clinics meet patient needs while building strong, sustainable operations.

This is a hands-on, clinic-facing role requiring regular in-person visits and travel between clinics throughout the Hamilton area.

Strengthen clinic operations: Improve workflows, scheduling, staffing and resource utilization. Help teams implement practical solutions that support efficient operations and an exceptional patient experience.
Support patient access: Partner with clinic leaders to align appointment availability, team capacity and provider coverage with patient demand. Help teams respond effectively to urgent and evolving scheduling needs.
Build strong, engaged teams: Partner with Clinic Managers and People & Culture to recruit, onboard, develop and retain great people. Encourage collaboration, address team challenges and create an environment where expectations are clear and people feel supported.

A demonstrated ability to build, develop and retain strong teams, including experience coaching managers and addressing team or performance challenges.
Strong business and financial acumen, with experience using KPIs, budgets and operational reporting to guide decisions and improve results.
A practical approach to problem-solving, with the ability to identify root causes, prioritize competing needs and implement sustainable improvements.
Excellent communication and relationship-building skills, with confidence partnering with Doctors, Clinic Managers and Support Office teams.
The ability to balance regional priorities with hands-on support tailored to individual clinics.
Sound judgment and adaptability when responding to changing patient demand, staffing needs and operational priorities.

The mission of this strategic role is to protect information assets, data, digital heritage, and production and broadcasting infrastructure across all platforms, while ensuring seamless, agile and uninterrupted media operations.

Chez Groupe INVESTIIR, on bâtit l'avenir des gens en simplifiant l'accès à la propriété. On structure le groupe pour sa prochaine étape : un comité de direction, des revenus récurrents, et des systèmes qui roulent sans le fondateur. Un responsable finance, une technicienne comptable, une responsable RH et un conseiller juridique interne. Le président garde une seule chose : la relation avec les banques et les investisseurs. Tu prépares les chiffres, il porte la relation.

À quelqu'un qui pense en comptabilité plutôt qu'en cash, ou qui préfère attendre que les chiffres lui arrivent.

jobs.title: Managing Director
jobs.description:
I've run Bodega Ridge since 2003. It's grown into three places on Galiano: the lodge and log cabins at Bodega Ridge, the waterfront cabins at Bodega Cove, and the Pink Geranium Café & Grocery. We host weddings and retreats, and we look after families and travellers who come for a few quiet days on the island.

I'm hiring a Managing Director to run the Collection. This is a new role for us. We've had general managers before, but this job is bigger. You'll make the day-to-day decisions, lead the team, be responsible for the numbers, and build what's next with me. I'll focus on development projects, including the spa and staff housing, and stay involved in sales and with guests at key moments. We'll agree on the budget and major investments together, and I'll be around when you need me.

What the job looks like here

A busy week might start with reviewing payroll and end with a wedding, a full house, and a pump that needs fixing. Spring through fall means longer days, evenings, and weekends. Sometimes you'll cover a shift or sort out a guest issue at 10 p.m. If you're hoping for a quieter pace, this probably isn't the right fit.

We also don't have many systems yet. Scheduling, ordering, maintenance, training and reporting all need to be set up, and that's your job. You'll build them, run the key decisions by me, and make them stick. You'll also build a team that knows who to call and what to do when things go sideways.

Get the different parts of the business working together. Make sure the cabins are ready for arrivals, the café and event teams know what's coming, and maintenance issues get dealt with. Keep weddings and retreats running smoothly, look after safety across the properties, and stay on good terms with our neighbours.
Build a team that can grow with us. Hire, train, and schedule staff, and give team leads the support and authority to run their areas. Put clear procedures in place so people know what's expected. Make time for the small things we care about, like remembering a guest's name or leaving a thoughtful note in a cabin.
Stay close to the numbers. Own the P&L, set budgets for each part of the business, and update forecasts as bookings change. Review hours, approve payroll, and match staffing to what's on the books. Keep an eye on pricing, labour, food costs, and margins. Tell me how we're doing, what's changed, and where you need a decision from me.
Build the next pieces at a pace we can handle. In your first year, help turn our new saunas into a wellness offering by working out how we'll staff, price, and run it. Take charge of the retreats we put on ourselves, from planning the program to making sure each one makes money.

Who I'm looking for

You've spent at least three years as a General Manager, Director of Operations, or in a similar role at a lodge, inn, resort, or boutique hotel. You've run both accommodations and food and beverage. You know how to hire and develop people, build a schedule for a busy weekend, and read a P&L well enough to decide what needs attention. You're comfortable overseeing payroll and can communicate clearly with staff, guests, vendors, and wedding planners, especially when things get busy. You use AI tools to work smarter, or you're keen to learn, and you'll bring the team along.

Experience with weddings, retreats, wellness, island or remote operations, or growing direct bookings would be helpful. Serving It Right, FOODSAFE, and first aid are assets.

You'll need to relocate to Galiano Island, hold a valid driver's licence, and be legally eligible to work in Canada.

Pay and benefits

Starting at C$110,000, depending on experience
C$20,000 target annual performance bonus tied to agreed operating and financial goals
Housing on Galiano Island included
Health benefits and a retention bonus

Send me a message with your résumé and a short note about a place you've helped run and what draws you to Bodega Ridge. No recruiters, please.

We welcome applicants of all backgrounds. If you need an accommodation during the hiring process, please let us know.

We own and operate payment systems that process hundreds of billions of dollars’ worth of payment transactions every business day. We convene ecosystem participants to discuss their multiple and diverse interests and ideas and to navigate industry-level challenges. We adhere to a set of values that are our north star:

Inspire trust, build community and enable change
.
Payments Canada — where our country connects

Our culture

With our people in mind, we have created a culture that fosters authenticity, collaboration, innovation and development. We empower one another, make meaningful contributions that not only impact the organization, but our country! We develop and nurture meaningful connections that drive innovation in our ecosystem. We are Payments Canada!

Do you want to make payments easier, smarter and safer for Canada? Join us today!

You need to work here if:

You love working with passionate, ambitious and collaborative colleagues.
You want to be challenged and lead unique initiatives.
You want to grow, develop and become a subject matter expert in your field.
You want your work to make an impact in your community and country .

Come and join us — where payments meet purpose!

What we are looking for

Reporting to the Chief Legal & Policy Officer, the Vice President, Compliance, Privacy and Bank of Canada Affairs is a senior-level executive and advisor to Payments Canada’s Executive Leadership Team on all matters related to compliance, privacy and the regulatory oversight relationship with the Bank of Canada.

Responsibilities of the position include:

Compliance Mandate:
Oversee Payments Canada’s compliance with laws and regulatory requirements to maintain legal compliance and uphold integrity.
Privacy Mandate:
Act as the designated Chief Privacy Officer for Payments Canada, accountable for compliance with privacy laws and regulations and for Payments Canada’s privacy management program.
Bank of Canada Affairs Mandate:
Responsible and accountable for managing the oversight relationship with the Bank of Canada, for the observance of the Bank of Canada risk-management standards for our designated payment systems, and Payments Canada’s obligations with regard to the Bank of Canada Oversight Agreement.

Duties and Responsibilities:

Compliance

Manage the corporate compliance function, exercising specialized knowledge of business processes, regulatory and corporate compliance requirements.

Develop, implement and maintain up to date an enterprise regulatory compliance management program, including systems, policies, procedures, structures and internal controls to ensure compliance with applicable laws, rules and regulations.
Develop the annual work plan (compliance, privacy and Bank of Canada Affairs) considering Payments Canada’s strategic objectives and risk profile; and periodically revising the plan in light of ongoing developments.
Provide reasonable assurance to senior management and the Board that there are effective and efficient policies and procedures in place, well understood and respected by all employees and that Payments Canada is in compliance with regulatory requirements.

Partner with business units to ensure compliance obligations are considered and integrated into new products or initiatives.

Oversee the implementation and maintenance of the corporate policy framework for compliance-related responsibilities and topics.

Act as designated recipient of anonymous complaints under Payments Canada’s Code of Conduct and Respect and Safety in the Work Place policy and work with Legal and Human Resources teams to assess and resolve complaints and issues, including conflicts of interest, raised by employees in relation to the Code of Conduct or Respect and Safety in the Work Place policy.
Review and provide recommendations to the President and CEO regarding enterprise compliance complaints.
Oversee the annual process for business unit confirmation of compliance with applicable laws and regulatory requirements.

Privacy

Act as the designated individual, Chief Privacy Officer (required by privacy legislation) accountable for compliance with privacy laws and regulations.
Develop and maintain Payments Canada’s privacy management program.
Implement strategies, policies and procedures to protect personal information in Payments Canada’s possession or custody, including conducting privacy impact assessments, when applicable.
Provide privacy related advice for the selection, development and implementation of new technological solutions, programs, projects and related processes.
Review and sign off on requests for information under the Access to Information Act .
Establish procedures to record and report breaches involving personal information, and respond to security breaches, complaints and inquiries.
Report and notify individuals in the event of a privacy breach.
Ensure training on privacy procedures and policies, and communication to employees on Payments Canada’s policies and procedures.

Oversee reporting of the execution of regulatory initiatives and priorities with a focus on quality and timeliness.
Review and provide input on annual system self-assessments, including seeking approval of self-assessments by the Board.

Attract and retain professionals with the skill sets and competencies needed to deliver Payments Canada’s strategic priorities.

Supporting others to develop and learn, recognizing one's own achievements and building an organizational culture where knowledge and growth are valued and rewarded.

Demonstrating confidence and realistic trust in one's own abilities. Understanding and managing your own emotions drives and the impact of self on others to minimize counterproductive actions, and instill trust and inspire others.

Seeing and synthesizing different sides of an issue, examining the full range of options and outcomes and building intellectual frameworks to guide analysis and action.

Using critical thinking, good business sense and organizational values to make decisions involving varying levels of risk and ambiguity.

Apply Business Acumen:
Continually seeking new ways to enhance performance, improve results and transform the business and the industry in which it operates.

What you need to be successful

Undergraduate degree in business, law or a related field.

You’ll build a deep understanding of trading and hedging strategies, provide effective challenge to the desks, and perform daily and periodic monitoring of positions, risk, profit and loss (P&L), and capital. new_jobs.description:
About YPO

YPO is a global leadership community of over 35,000 chief executives from more than 140 countries. YPO brings together extraordinary leaders who are committed to becoming better leaders and better people. The organization provides a platform for the leaders to connect, learn, and grow through shared experiences, rich learning programs, and meaningful relationships. Members benefit from a supportive community that fosters personal, business, family and community growth.

Supporting these members is a world-class management team of more than 450 associates, spanning over 25 countries. Our organization is based in Dallas, Texas, with many associates working virtually and outside of the United States. Together, our team of global associates works to create a truly Only-in-YPO experience for our members.

Location & Onsite Expectations

Candidates based in the Dallas–Fort Worth area are strongly preferred. This role will require an onsite presence, with the specific number of days per week to be determined. Highly qualified candidates based elsewhere in the U.S. and Canada may also be considered. C andidates in Canada must reside in British Columbia, Ontario, Alberta or Nova Scotia
as YPO is not an employer in other Canadian provinces.

About the Opportunity

At YPO, we're reimagining how technology can better connect, engage, and empower leaders across our global community.

We're seeking an experienced Product Design Director to build and shape our product design function from the ground up, establishing a unified design vision across our evolving digital ecosystem.

This is an opportunity to make a lasting impact on how our members experience YPO. You'll define the design principles, systems, and standards that bring consistency across our platforms, guide the evolution of our mobile and digital experiences, and help shape how AI creates more intuitive, personalized, and meaningful interactions.

We're looking for a leader who combines deep UX and product design expertise with the ability to build teams, influence product strategy, and turn complex challenges into thoughtful, scalable solutions. Someone with a strong point of view who can balance innovation with execution, navigate competing priorities, and bring stakeholders together around a shared vision.

Reporting to our Chief Product Officer, you'll partner closely with Product, Engineering, Data, and business leaders to establish the foundation for design excellence at YPO while remaining hands-on as the function grows.

What You'll Do

Build and Lead Our Design Function: Establish and grow an in-house product design team, developing the frameworks, processes, and practices that enable high-quality design across multiple product teams.
Establish a Unified Design Vision: Define a cohesive design strategy, scalable design systems, and consistent interaction standards across YPO's web, mobile, and digital experiences.
Shape Our Digital Future: Guide the evolution of our mobile application ecosystem and digital platforms, translating emerging opportunities into intuitive, connected member experiences.
Champion Research-Driven Design: Lead user research, usability testing, and persona development, using qualitative insights and product analytics to identify problems, validate solutions, and inform product decisions.
Advance AI-First Experiences: Help define how AI enhances the member experience through conversational interfaces, intelligent agents, personalization, and adaptive design, with an emphasis on transparency, trust, and user control.
Influence Product Direction: Partner with Product, Engineering, Data, and business stakeholders to navigate competing priorities, advocate for user-centered decisions, and align teams around a shared vision.
Lead as a Player-Coach: Combine strategic leadership with hands-on design, prototyping, critique, and problem-solving while mentoring designers and elevating the team's capabilities.
Drive Design Excellence: Champion accessibility, thoughtful interactions, and measurable product outcomes, ensuring experiences are scalable, inclusive, and consistent with YPO's mission.

What We're Looking For

10+ years of product design experience, including 5+ years leading and developing design teams, ideally at the Director level.
Demonstrated success building or scaling product design functions, establishing design systems, and setting design standards across complex digital products.
Deep expertise in UX, interaction design, user research, usability testing, and translating customer needs into intuitive, scalable solutions.
Strong understanding of Apple's Human Interface Guidelines and Google's Material Design principles, with experience designing for iOS, Android, and web platforms.
Proven experience taking digital products from early discovery through launch, including 0–1 product development and measurable business or user outcomes.
Experience designing and delivering AI-powered products or features, with an understanding of LLMs, conversational interfaces, personalization, and responsible AI design.
Strong leadership and stakeholder management.

The Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) team is the backbone and the future-forward arm of CBC/Radio-Canada. Our purpose is to constantly innovate to evolve and maintain the Corporation’s technologies and infrastructure. We are the people that make stuff work. We make connections between media content, systems, people and places. We are the space in between.

A place with purpose. CBC/Radio-Canada has always been a highly regarded pioneer of media technology — not just in Canada, but around the world. Role Vision and Impact

The Senior Director, Information Security and End-User Technology, serves as CBC/Radio-Canada’s Chief Information Security Officer (CISO). A strategic, visionary and collaborative leader, the CISO defines, implements and drives the overarching vision for cybersecurity, risk management and technological resilience across all corporate environments.

The mission of this strategic role is to protect information assets, data, digital heritage, and production and broadcasting infrastructure across all platforms, while ensuring seamless, agile and uninterrupted media operations.
The Senior Director optimally balances rigorous security architecture governance with the flexibility that creative, journalistic and technical teams need to innovate and broadcast without disruption.

Operating at a senior executive level, the CISO regularly briefs and advises the Board of Directors (BoD),
the Audit Committee,

Strategic Vision, Leadership and Executive Relations

Develop, champion and execute an enterprise-wide cybersecurity strategy aligned with the Corporation’s business mission, risk profile and digital transformation.

Foster a “Security by Design” culture and establish security architecture governance frameworks that keep operational and production workflows running smoothly while proactively managing risk.
Anticipate technology trends and lead the secure integration of artificial intelligence (AI/GenAI) and automation into business processes and security defences across the organization.

Securing IT, Cloud, Distribution and Broadcast/Operational Technology (OT) Environments

Define and continuously adapt the security strategy across the entire technology landscape, including corporate IT infrastructure, cloud systems, end-user environments, and critical production, broadcast and network infrastructure.
Ensure the resilience of content acquisition, processing and distribution workflows against threats targeting the media sector and critical infrastructure.

Governance, Risk, Compliance and AI Governance

Oversee the governance function responsible for developing, maintaining and enforcing policies, standards, security architecture principles, exception management and industry frameworks (e.g., NIST, ISO 27001, AI frameworks).
Lead the third-party and partner risk management program (covering vendors and technology contracts) in close collaboration with the Legal Services and Procurement teams.
Co-develop a governance, compliance and ethical framework for the enterprise-wide use of AI and generative AI, assessing specific risks throughout their life cycle.
Ensure strict compliance with applicable laws and regulations (e.g., Quebec’s Law 25, GDPR and sector-specific requirements).
Drive a cybersecurity culture and awareness program focused on lasting behaviour change across the organization.

Defence Operations, SOC and Crisis Management

Direct major security incident response operations and lead technology crisis management, from detection to full business recovery.
Oversee regular penetration testing, vulnerability assessments and cyberattack simulation exercises across IT, broadcast and distribution environments.

Identity and End-User Technology

Collaborate closely with the End-User Technology teams to align security with a modern, efficient and intuitive employee experience.

Financial Management and Team Engagement

Lead with the heart.

Depuis Saint-Hubert, on développe et on vend des terrains et des chalets dans Lanaudière et les Laurentides — et on est verticalement intégrés : on achète le terrain, on le lotit, on construit les rues, on bâtit les chalets, on les vend et on accompagne nos clients jusqu'à la location. On structure le groupe pour sa prochaine étape : un comité de direction, des revenus récurrents, et des systèmes qui roulent sans le fondateur. Un responsable finance, une technicienne comptable, une responsable RH et un conseiller juridique interne. Le président garde une seule chose : la relation avec les banques et les investisseurs. Tu prépares les chiffres, il porte la relation.

À quelqu'un qui pense en comptabilité plutôt qu'en cash, ou qui préfère attendre que les chiffres lui arrivent.

Un partage des profits : chaque tranche de 100 000 $ de profit net ajusté (après impôts, intérêts, comptes en retard et fonds de prévoyance) verse 10 000 $ au pool, divisé en parts égales entre tous les employés admissibles — dès le premier dollar, sans plafond

I've run Bodega Ridge since 2003. It's grown into three places on Galiano: the lodge and log cabins at Bodega Ridge, the waterfront cabins at Bodega Cove, and the Pink Geranium Café & Grocery. We host weddings and retreats, and we look after families and travellers who come for a few quiet days on the island.

I'm hiring a Managing Director to run the Collection. This is a new role for us. We've had general managers before, but this job is bigger. You'll make the day-to-day decisions, lead the team, be responsible for the numbers, and build what's next with me. I'll focus on development projects, including the spa and staff housing, and stay involved in sales and with guests at key moments. We'll agree on the budget and major investments together, and I'll be around when you need me.

What the job looks like here

A busy week might start with reviewing payroll and end with a wedding, a full house, and a pump that needs fixing. Spring through fall means longer days, evenings, and weekends. Sometimes you'll cover a shift or sort out a guest issue at 10 p.m. If you're hoping for a quieter pace, this probably isn't the right fit.

We also don't have many systems yet. Scheduling, ordering, maintenance, training and reporting all need to be set up, and that's your job. You'll build them, run the key decisions by me, and make them stick. You'll also build a team that knows who to call and what to do when things go sideways.

Get the different parts of the business working together. Make sure the cabins are ready for arrivals, the café and event teams know what's coming, and maintenance issues get dealt with. Keep weddings and retreats running smoothly, look after safety across the properties, and stay on good terms with our neighbours.
Build a team that can grow with us. Hire, train, and schedule staff, and give team leads the support and authority to run their areas. Put clear procedures in place so people know what's expected. Make time for the small things we care about, like remembering a guest's name or leaving a thoughtful note in a cabin.
Stay close to the numbers. Own the P&L, set budgets for each part of the business, and update forecasts as bookings change. Review hours, approve payroll, and match staffing to what's on the books. Keep an eye on pricing, labour, food costs, and margins. Tell me how we're doing, what's changed, and where you need a decision from me.
Build the next pieces at a pace we can handle. In your first year, help turn our new saunas into a wellness offering by working out how we'll staff, price, and run it. Take charge of the retreats we put on ourselves, from planning the program to making sure each one makes money.

Who I'm looking for

You've spent at least three years as a General Manager, Director of Operations, or in a similar role at a lodge, inn, resort, or boutique hotel. You've run both accommodations and food and beverage. You know how to hire and develop people, build a schedule for a busy weekend, and read a P&L well enough to decide what needs attention. You're comfortable overseeing payroll and can communicate clearly with staff, guests, vendors, and wedding planners, especially when things get busy. You use AI tools to work smarter, or you're keen to learn, and you'll bring the team along.

Experience with weddings, retreats, wellness, island or remote operations, or growing direct bookings would be helpful. Serving It Right, FOODSAFE, and first aid are assets.

You'll need to relocate to Galiano Island, hold a valid driver's licence, and be legally eligible to work in Canada.

C$20,000 target annual performance bonus tied to agreed operating and financial goals
Housing on Galiano Island included
Health benefits and a retention bonus

Send me a message with your résumé and a short note about a place you've helped run and what draws you to Bodega Ridge. No recruiters, please.

Inspire trust, build community and enable change
.

We are Payments Canada!

You love working with passionate, ambitious and collaborative colleagues.

You want your work to make an impact in your community and country .

Compliance Mandate:
Oversee Payments Canada’s compliance with laws and regulatory requirements to maintain legal compliance and uphold integrity.
Privacy Mandate:
Act as the designated Chief Privacy Officer for Payments Canada, accountable for compliance with privacy laws and regulations and for Payments Canada’s privacy management program.
Bank of Canada Affairs Mandate:
Responsible and accountable for managing the oversight relationship with the Bank of Canada, for the observance of the Bank of Canada risk-management standards for our designated payment systems, and Payments Canada’s obligations with regard to the Bank of Canada Oversight Agreement.

Compliance

Manage the corporate compliance function, exercising specialized knowledge of business processes, regulatory and corporate compliance requirements.
Maintain effective relationships with Payments Canada’s regulators, including the Bank of Canada and Department of Finance, in cooperation with the Government Relations team, to support Payments Canada’s regulatory compliance obligations under the Canadian Payments Act and Payment Clearing and Settlement Act .
Develop, implement and maintain up to date an enterprise regulatory compliance management program, including systems, policies, procedures, structures and internal controls to ensure compliance with applicable laws, rules and regulations.
Develop the annual work plan (compliance, privacy and Bank of Canada Affairs) considering Payments Canada’s strategic objectives and risk profile; and periodically revising the plan in light of ongoing developments.
Provide reasonable assurance to senior management and the Board that there are effective and efficient policies and procedures in place, well understood and respected by all employees and that Payments Canada is in compliance with regulatory requirements.
Foster a culture of ethics throughout the organization, promoting awareness and understanding of compliance requirements and expectations.
Promote compliance input and leadership to business partners across the organization, including Human Resources, Legal, Payment Operations, Payment Products, Security, Risk and Policy.
Partner with business units to ensure compliance obligations are considered and integrated into new products or initiatives.

Oversee the implementation and maintenance of the corporate policy framework for compliance-related responsibilities and topics.
Provide input and guidance on corporate policy framework and training programs to support and educate employees on compliance-related responsibilities and topics.

Oversee the annual process for business unit confirmation of compliance with applicable laws and regulatory requirements.

Develop and maintain Payments Canada’s privacy management program.
